executive_summary: NZD/USD is 0.56142 in the gated store (spotDate 2026-10-02). Under this pair's quoting convention, a rising number means a stronger kiwi. The pair is down 4.55% over one month, 1.12% over three months, 3.57% over six months and 1.75% over a year. Its close sits at the 4th percentile of the 52-week closing range, 31 pips above the intraday 52-week low of 0.55832 and 16 pips above the top of the series' strongest support band, 0.5556-0.5598, which has six touches. The main story is a rate gap that now runs against the kiwi. The OCR is 2.75% against a Fed effective rate of 3.875%, so the kiwi pays 112.5bp to hold. A rolled long costs about 4.9 pips a month at the CME roll premium of 106.6bp. Both central banks decide on 2026-10-28, so the differential cannot move before then. Two bilateral features are missing from either standalone dossier. First, the two decisions land on the same day, so an RBNZ hike can be cancelled out by the Fed within hours. Second, oil compounds rather than offsets for this pair: $100 Brent hurts the importer leg and helps the exporter leg, so it pushes the pair down twice. The settled verdict is Bearish tactically (conviction 3, score -0.4398) and Bullish strategically (conviction 2, score +0.1164). The pass-2 level work does not argue with the direction. It argues with where to enter: shorting at spot means selling into a six-touch floor with 20-day realised vol compressed to 5.9%. So the tactical short is built by selling rallies into 0.5645-0.5690, with a 0.5745 stop and targets of 0.5560 and 0.5450. The strategic long is built in the 0.5560-0.5600 band after 2026-10-28, with a stop on a weekly close below 0.5480 and targets of 0.5760 and 0.5980. The caveat is that kiwi shorts have been squeezed hard before: from a record leveraged-fund short in July, the pair rallied 5.3% in six weeks.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is -112.5bp: the OCR at 2.75% against a Fed effective rate of 3.875% (target range 3.75-4.00%), per the gated rate block. A long NZD/USD therefore pays carry, and the cached futures roll premium of 106.6bp annualised confirms that a rolled long position bleeds roughly the differential less a small basis. The direction of travel over four weeks is the problem rather than the level: both central banks announce on the same day, 2026-10-28, so the differential cannot move until that date, and the two tails are asymmetric for the pair. An RBNZ hike to 3.00% alongside a Fed hold narrows the gap by 25bp and is the single most likely outcome, but it is also the outcome most nearly in the price, whereas an RBNZ hold against hawkish expectations or a Fed hike would each widen the gap. Transmission runs through carry and through the front-end spread: with the US two-year sitting roughly 90bp above the effective funds rate and the New Zealand two-year roughly 117bp above the OCR, both front ends already discount tightening, so the pair's four-week rate signal is the negative carry itself plus the asymmetry of the October surprise distribution.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the differential is more likely to narrow than to widen, and that is the strongest pair-positive force in this analysis. The RBNZ is early in a tightening cycle begun in July from 2.25%, with bank paths clustered at 3.00-3.25% by year-end and some houses higher; the Fed's September projections put the funds rate at 4.1% at both end-2026 and end-2027, which is a plateau within 25bp of the current level. If the RBNZ delivers one more hike than the Fed, the gap compresses from -112.5bp toward -87.5bp or -75bp. The decision that would do it is 2026-12-09, when the RBNZ publishes a new Monetary Policy Statement with an updated OCR track and the FOMC publishes a new SEP on the same day - the cleanest scheduled test of the convergence thesis in the window. Transmission is through the front-end spread rather than carry: the pair does not need positive carry to rise, it needs the market to mark the relative path, and a December RBNZ track lifted toward 3.50% against an unchanged Fed dot is exactly that event. The offset is that the New Zealand two-year already discounts more tightening than the RBNZ has published, so part of the convergence is in the curve; what is not in the curve is the relative stop - a Fed that has finished while the RBNZ has not.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth differential is wide and running in the dollar's favour. US Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% annualised with August payrolls at 162,000 against a 55,000 consensus, ISM manufacturing at 54.5 and unemployment steady at 4.1%; New Zealand grew 0.2% q/q in Q2 with unemployment at 5.6%, a nine-year high, and real gross national disposable income falling 0.4% on the terms-of-trade loss. The inflation differential points the other way in headline terms - New Zealand CPI at 4.1% against US CPI at 3.4% - but the composition reverses the signal: New Zealand's overshoot is tradables and fuel with sectoral-factor core at 2.7%, while US core PCE at 3.0% sits above the Fed's comfort and keeps the front end supported. Asymmetric data sensitivity matters here: the US releases monthly high-frequency data that move the dollar leg repeatedly inside the window, whereas New Zealand's swing print is a single quarterly CPI on 2026-10-21. Transmission is through relative real activity surprise into relative front-end pricing, and on current momentum the US side is the one more likely to add to yields.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the inflation gap closes in a way that does not help the pair. New Zealand's overshoot is fuel-driven and the RBNZ expects inflation back inside the 1-3% band by mid-2027, so the annual rate falls as the 2026 fuel spike drops out, which shortens the hiking cycle that the strategic rates case depends on. On the US side core PCE has eased from 3.3% to 3.0% and the Fed's own projections take it to 2.5% in 2027, so the disinflation is symmetric; what is not symmetric is the growth and income backdrop. New Zealand is absorbing a 9.0% quarterly terms-of-trade loss with a flat housing market, unemployment at 5.6% that the RBNZ expects to improve only marginally, and wage growth of 2.0%, while the US runs a roughly 0.9pp growth advantage over its own trading partners with corporate profits rising. A central bank hiking into stagnant real incomes is a weaker currency support than a central bank plateauing in a 2%-plus economy. Confidence is only 52 because the US consumer is visibly straining - confidence at 81.9, Michigan at 48.1 - and because the latest New Zealand CPI print predates the tactical freshness window.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a high-beta versus haven pairing, and the current regime is the one in which that pairing underperforms: equity volatility is calm while credit is repricing. The VIX closed near 16 at roughly the 34th percentile of its year, the S&P 500 is up double digits on the year, but the US high-yield option-adjusted spread widened 42-59bp in a month to the 300-324bp area, at or near the top of its one-year range, and investment-grade spreads are at the 94th percentile. That is a rates-led tightening of financial conditions rather than an equity drawdown, and it is precisely the configuration in which a small, deficit-running, thinly traded currency loses to the dollar without needing a risk-off shock. The dollar's measured correlation to equities is mildly negative and to the ten-year yield mildly positive, so rising yields push both legs of this pair the same way. The cross-asset tails are a Gulf settlement that compresses oil and risk premia together (pair-positive) and a credit event taking high-yield beyond 400bp (pair-negative); inside four weeks the second looks the more likely given where US long yields sit.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the risk complex is genuinely two-sided for this pair and the tails roughly cancel. The bear case is a continuation of the rates-led squeeze: US long yields above 5%, credit spreads already widened from tight levels, and an energy shock that keeps headline inflation sticky - all of which punish the kiwi leg more than the dollar leg. The bull case is that the shock is energy-specific and reversible: China's manufacturing PMI has returned to expansion at 50.1 with output at a nine-month high, Middle East crude shipments are approaching pre-war levels, and a negotiated reopening would compress oil and risk premia simultaneously, which is a double positive for a commodity-importing high-beta currency against the dollar. Neither dossier carries a directional six-month risk view - both resolve to Neutral - and combining two Neutrals through a bilateral lens does not manufacture a signal. Credit at roughly the 72nd percentile of five years and the VIX at the 37th are repricing, not crisis, so the honest reading is that this factor contributes nothing strategically.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three bilateral factors are weighted differently. First, consensus treats RBNZ hikes as currency-supportive in the conventional way, whereas we note the kiwi is now the lower-yielding leg at -112.5bp and that the New Zealand two-year already discounts more tightening than the RBNZ has published, so the hikes buy less than they appear to. Third, most of the cited bank paths predate the September dollar repricing and the Fed's move to 3.75-4.00%, so they are not reacting to the current differential at all. Where we do agree with consensus is on direction over the medium term, and on the mechanism: a Fed at its plateau while the RBNZ is still moving.

The strategic risk is Brent above $110, which would widen the New Zealand deficit, hand the dollar a terms-of-trade gain and push the +0.1164 score back below the Neutral boundary.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge by -0.56 of score, and the divergence is mechanical rather than a hedge. Three factors change sign. Policy and Rates is Bearish tactically because the differential is locked at -112.5bp until 2026-10-28 and the pair pays carry to wait, but Bullish strategically because the RBNZ can out-hike a Fed whose own projections show a plateau through 2027. Fiscal and Event Risk are Neutral tactically for want of a catalyst but Bullish strategically once the 2026-11-03 midterms and the 2026-12-11 funding expiry enter the window. Risk Appetite and Market Structure run the other way, Bearish tactically on the rates-led credit widening and the doubled downside skew, Neutral strategically because the Gulf binary and a flat vol surface carry no multi-month direction. The asymmetry in conviction matters: the tactical case is broad but driven by one mechanism, while the strategic case is narrow and clears its threshold by 1.6 points.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 2026-10-28 RBNZ Monetary Policy Review and FOMC, which land on the same day and are the first date on which the differential can move at all; the thesis is then confirmed or broken on 2026-12-09, when the RBNZ publishes a new OCR track and the FOMC a new SEP, again on the same day.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: The two horizons are sequential rather than contradictory: the tactical bearish phase runs into the 2026-10-28 cluster, and the strategic bullish phase requires the 2026-12-09 pair of projection rounds to validate rate convergence. Navigating the switch means not carrying the tactical view through the December decisions and not establishing the strategic view before the front-end event premium around 2026-10-28 has decayed. A failure of the RBNZ to hike at either October or December collapses both the inflection and the strategic case. Pass-2 level implication: the two horizons meet at one price band - the tactical short's T1 (0.5560) and the strategic long's entry zone (0.5560-0.5600) are both the six-touch support. Cover the short and start accumulating the long in that band after 2026-10-28; use a weekly close below 0.5480 as the shared line where the tactical view has won and the strategic view has lost; use a daily close above 0.5730 as the line where the tactical view has lost and the strategic long should already be on.

A second consecutive decline would confirm that the one offset to the oil-driven terms-of-trade loss is fading, removing the support that holds Factor 5 at Neutral tactically and tilting the pair lower into the event cluster.

With fuel prices having risen through September the risk is an upside surprise that locks in an October hike and forces the 21,655-contract asset-manager swing to begin reversing. A print at or below 3.6% would do the opposite and remove the base leg's only domestic support.

The first date on which the -112.5bp differential can move. A hike to 3.00% narrows it by 25bp and is the pair's main scheduled upside; the complication is that it lands the same day as the FOMC, so the kiwi's own shock is filtered through the dollar within hours. Reported pricing ranges from roughly 30% (consistent with the RBNZ's own published track) to roughly 75% (after Governor Breman's oil remarks), which makes this the most genuinely two-sided date in the window. Post-payload reporting notes the RBNZ may still hike on 28 October even though its own September track had October as a pause.

Control of Congress determines how the 2026-12-11 funding expiry is negotiated and therefore whether the quote leg's fiscal risk crystallises inside the strategic window. September polling projected 64 of 120 seats for the governing bloc against 56, close enough that coalition formation could run into late November. A clear result is neutral for the pair; a drawn-out negotiation adds a domestic risk premium to the base leg, and a change of government implies looser fiscal policy that the RBNZ would have to lean against - mildly supportive for rates, mildly negative for risk premium.

catalysts.rationale: The decisive event for the strategic thesis. The September track peaks at 3.28% and its Q4 average is consistent with a December hike; lifting the peak toward 3.50% would convert rate convergence from forecast to published policy. This is the dated claim on which the Factor 1 and Factor 6 strategic stances rest, and a track lifted only to 3.25-3.30% would reprice the base leg lower.

catalysts.rationale: The other half of the convergence test, on the same day. catalysts.event: Expiry of the US continuing resolution (government funding deadline)
catalysts.rationale: The quote leg's only dated sovereign-risk event in the window, landing two days after both projection rounds and inside the year-end funding turn. A shutdown would revive the governance debate Fitch cited when affirming AA+ and would distort the Treasury General Account at the worst moment of the funding calendar - a dollar-negative that supports the pair, with the caveat that a disorderly turn could briefly push the dollar to the left side of the smile instead.

invalidators.condition: Squeeze through the four-touch band: NZD/USD posts a daily close above 0.5730 before 2026-10-28
invalidators.mechanism: That close reclaims the top of the four-touch September breakdown band and the 0.5700 trend-ending level. It would mean the one-week asset-manager swing and the record-speed dollar build are unwinding together, and the July 2026 analogue shows that run extends several big figures.

invalidators.condition: Hawkish double: NZ Q3 CPI prints at or above 4.2% y/y on 2026-10-21 and the RBNZ hikes to 3.00% while the FOMC holds on 2026-10-28
invalidators.mechanism: Both parts of the bearish rates logic would fail at once: the differential narrows to -87.5bp on the only date it can move, and the dollar-side offset fails to arrive the same day.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Stats NZ CPI; the RBNZ and FOMC statements

invalidators.condition: Convergence fails: the RBNZ holds at 2.75% on 2026-10-28, or its 2026-12-09 track peaks at or below 3.30% while the same-day SEP lifts the 2027 Fed dot to 4.4% or higher
invalidators.mechanism: The differential would widen instead of compress, removing the +0.1344 Factor 1 contribution that carries the whole strategic score.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: RBNZ OCR and track; FOMC SEP 2027 median

invalidators.condition: Floor breaks: NZD/USD posts a weekly close below 0.5480
invalidators.mechanism: That close takes out the six-touch 0.5556-0.5598 band and the 0.5500 round number, below which no computed support exists. The pair would then be trading the oil-driven income transfer rather than rate convergence, and the strategic entry zone would be gone.

invalidators.condition: Oil compounding: Brent holds above $115 for ten sessions
invalidators.mechanism: Oil moves both legs against the pair at once: the NZ import bill and current account worsen while US terms of trade and Fed inflation pressure strengthen. External Balance would outweigh rate convergence.

invalidators.condition: Gulf settlement: Brent falls below $85 for five sessions on a US-Iran settlement
invalidators.mechanism: A settlement reverses the compounding mechanism in the pair's favour on both legs and removes the dollar's haven and terms-of-trade premium.

invalidators.condition: Front-end spread compresses early: the NZ-US 2-year spread narrows inside -70bp before 2026-10-28 (currently about -86bp: NZ 3.92% vs US 4.78% on 2026-10-01)
invalidators.mechanism: It would show the real-yield channel behind five of the six bearish tactical factors reversing before the differential can formally move.

assumptions: Price payload quoted verbatim: dataPoints 130; dateRange 2026-04-03 to 2026-10-02; spot 0.56142; spotDate 2026-10-02; computationRange 2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02 (4899 weekday bars).

dataQuality: 'NZD/USD: only 11 resistance / 1 support zones met the 2-touch threshold - supplement with round numbers and note the shortfall'; 4899 weekday bars in the store (1006 weekly, 460 monthly); 130 daily bars passed downstream (2026-04-03 to 2026-10-02), the 1-6 month strategic horizon.

spotDate (2026-10-02) is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date. Every level, pip distance, percentage, forward and scenario is computed against 0.56142. Web commentary reporting later trade near and below 0.5600 on 2026-10-05 is cited only as qualitative technical context and is not used in any calculation.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes over the full store. Realised vol is annualised on 252 days. ATR(14) is 45 pips. Zone distances are the payload's figures measured from spot to each zone's midpoint; distances used in trade construction are measured to zone boundaries and labelled as such. The support-zone shortfall is handled with the 0.5600 and 0.5500 round numbers and the 52-week intraday low.

The two-pass split: factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings, the consensus block and the cross-horizon block are the pass-1 Direction Verdict carried through unchanged. Pass 1 scored without the price payload and the payload was not used to revise any of them. Pass-2 content (market context, carry and forwards, levels, scenarios, risk/reward, path, conviction ladders, invalidators, signposts, expression) is labelled; where pass 2 disagrees, as on tactical entry location, the disagreement is stated in prose and the verdict stands.

The policy differential is -112.5bp using the payload rate block and the Fed effective midpoint. annualised_carry_bps is reported as -112.5 (a long pays), consistent with the carry-to-vol ratios in the report (-0.130 on 8.651%); the CME roll premium of 106.6bp is reported separately as the funding premium. The payload's 10-year yields are monthly vintages dated 2026-08-01 and are not quoted as live levels.

The NZ-US 2-year spread uses the dossiers' live prints: NZ 3.92% (2026-10-01) and US 4.78% (2026-10-01, quote dossier). The base dossier's 4.92% US print dated 2026-09-28 gives -100bp; both are disclosed.

Forwards are derived from the CME 6NZ6->6NH7 roll premium of 106.6bp on an actual/365 basis; they are not quoted outrights. The premium includes cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated without an OIS curve.

Implied vol and risk reversals are gated CME values observed 2026-09-30 at 36.7, 99.7 and 155.7 days. pair_3m_iv is 8.651% at 99.7 days. No one-year IV percentile is available (CME history starts 2026-08-21); iv_percentile of 70 is the base dossier's figure within 26 observations.

CFTC percentiles: the report describes both legs as 'at the 44th-56th percentile' and the aggregate dollar long as around the 44th percentile of cached weeks; base_cftc_percentile is therefore entered as 56 and quote_cftc_percentile as 44. range_52w_percentile uses the intraday range (6th); the closing-range percentile is the 4th.

Scenario probabilities follow the framework's 50/25/25 convention, with expected values computed explicitly. Position sizing is illustrative: 0.50% of capital at risk for conviction 3 and 0.30% for conviction 2, pip value US$10 per NZ$100k.
Bilateral trade is taken verbatim from the IMF DOTS block for 2024, NZ-reported net +$0.5bn.

Aggregator surveys are lower-grade sources than primary bank research. Bank forecasts older than 60 days (ANZ in May, Rabobank in April, ING) are used only as context. The July 2026 record leveraged-fund short and subsequent rally are cited from web research and checked against the price store (0.5678 on 2026-07-07 to 0.59795 on 2026-08-21).

Dossier dates were not stated in the report; base_dossier_date and quote_dossier_date are set to the 2026-10-01 valuation date. Catalyst and factor citations marked 'dossier-sourced' or 'None incremental' are represented as empty arrays. Dossier-sourced catalysts and factor-level data have no numbered citation in the list.
